interface: Fixed q supplied, one raw path over 0 plus q fully observed event marks; stationary Markov renewal kernel with finite pi-weighted mean; no uniform mean bound or mixing bound.

claims.claim: Uniform bounded-span colored pool prior plus separate allzero option, uniform anchor/start mark, and outgoing-row urn draws stopping on empty current row defines a proper full-support block code despite unused other rows.
Exact target-pool mass and row multinomial bounds imply P_N(x)/Q_N(x)<=q K_N N uniformly, so block redundancy<=log K_N+log q+log N, with logK_N<=log2+2q sqrt(2N).
For observed marks the ordered-prefix probability is a row falling-factorial product with a single last-row tail moment; no Euler-trail constraints are imposed on unused pools.
DP over total span and q row totals exactly compiles fixed-horizon prefix marginals in O(q^2 N^{q+3}) integer operations.
Every grouped prefix denominator divides N!, and H_N=q K_N N! q_N is integer of O_q(N log N) bits; exact suffix-average output can require O_q(n^2 log n) bits.

Stationary countdown/next-mark capping to qN+1 initial values bounds the memory sum by log(qN+1), including reducible kernels and infinite uncapped-state entropy; fixed-Q_N suffix averaging gives uniform O_q(n^-1/2) expected terminal KL risk in conservative O_q(n^{q+6}log^2 n) bit time.
For each fixed q, the binary stationary renewal subclass and HJW source lower bound supply a matching n^-1/2 minimax order by KL data processing; no uniform q-dependence or sharp constant is claimed.

claims.claim: Independent exact finite diagnostics passed 3099 prefix equalities, 1157 categorical normalizations and 6578 stationary regret checks for q=1,2,3, exercising unused pools and reducible mark chains.

Garivier 2006 primary thesis p85 Thm22 shows CTW renewal redundancy Theta(sqrt(n) log n), while Thm23 concerns a Markov chain on unbounded interarrival-time states and has Theta(n^{2/3} log n) CTW redundancy; these do not establish priority for this exact interface.

not_claimed: polynomial time jointly in unbounded q and n
